name: Rest-vs-urgency situational fade
thesis: Teams eliminated from contention (playoff probability <5% per NGS) may rest starters late; the market prices reputation, not motivation.
signal_inputs: NGS playoff probability (S06); official injury/rest designations (S01)
data_required: NGS trends + injury report + closing spread history
why_it_might_work: Motivation is a real, documented coaching behaviour; rest designations appear in the official report.
what_would_kill_it: If playoff-probability-driven rest is already fully priced, edge is zero, and sample is tiny.

name: Depth-string deficiency fade (defense)
thesis: When a defence loses a starter and the next man up is 2nd-or-3rd string at a premium position, opponent scoring rises more than the line implies.
signal_inputs: Official injury report game status (S01) + official club depth chart (S11/S12)
data_required: Injury report + per-club depth charts + closing lines
why_it_might_work: Depth is a published fact; the join between 'Out' and 'who replaces him' is objective.
what_would_kill_it: Depth charts are club-published and 'unofficial' by their own labelling; they can lag reality.

name: Depth-string deficiency fade (offense, O-line first)
thesis: O-line attrition is the highest-leverage offensive injury because it degrades every skill player at once.
signal_inputs: S01 game status filtered to T/G/C + S11 depth strings
data_required: Injury report + depth charts + team total history
why_it_might_work: Sacks-taken vs PPG correlation measured at r=-0.621 (R2 38.6%), so pressure does move scoring.
what_would_kill_it: Positional criticality is not officially published; any weighting is our assumption.

name: Pass-efficiency momentum vs opponent pass defence
thesis: Pair offence passing Y/A with opponent passing Y/A allowed; extreme mismatches may not be fully priced.
signal_inputs: S03 offense pass YPA; S04 defense pass YPA
why_it_might_work: Measured: off pass Y/A vs PPG r=0.685 (R2 46.9%).
what_would_kill_it: Extremely well-known signal; expected to be priced.

name: Turnover-regression fade
thesis: Defensive interceptions are volatile. Teams winning on turnovers should regress; fade the team whose record is turnover-driven.
data_required: Interception data + closing lines + multi-season history
blocking_gate: G3 + G6 (needs multiple seasons to prove regression)
why_it_might_work: Measured: def INT vs points allowed r=-0.561, i.e. turnovers do correlate with scoring in-season.
what_would_kill_it: Requires multi-season data to separate luck from skill; one snapshot cannot.

name: Rush-efficiency trap avoidance (negative strategy)
thesis: Do NOT build a signal on rushing Y/A: in this snapshot it explains 0.1% of scoring variance.
what_would_kill_it: Already killed by our own data. Kept on the board so nobody rebuilds it.

name: Two-leg same-game stack (QB yards + WR1 yards)
thesis: Same-game legs are positively correlated, so the true joint probability exceeds the naive product and a standard parlay price can be +EV.
data_required: Player-level game logs, both legs, same game
blocking_gate: G1 (no player data) + G7 (no event-level rho)
why_it_might_work: Computed: at rho=0.40 a two-leg -110 parlay moves from -8.9% EV to +15.0% EV.
what_would_kill_it: Sportsbooks price correlated same-game parlays with their own correlation model; the edge may be exactly zero after their adjustment.

name: Two-leg negative-correlation fade (RB rushing + opposing QB)
thesis: Game-script legs are negatively correlated: a heavy rushing game suppresses opponent passing volume.
why_it_might_work: Computed: at rho=-0.40 a two-leg parlay is -32.8% EV versus -8.9% at rho=0. Standard pricing badly misprices these.
what_would_kill_it: If the book already applies a negative-correlation haircut, the 'find' disappears.

name: Injury-news latency (first-mover on official report)
thesis: The official report drops on a fixed deadline; acting inside the window between publication and line adjustment may capture value.
signal_inputs: S10 filing deadlines; S01 report content
data_required: Injury report timestamps + tick-level line history
why_it_might_work: The deadlines are officially published, so the timing is knowable in advance.
what_would_kill_it: Requires sub-minute line data and is a speed game, not a modelling game. Likely unwinnable for us.

name: Weather-and-total interaction
thesis: Wind and precipitation move totals; if the market under-adjusts, unders in high-wind games may be +EV.
signal_inputs: Not ingested — no official weather feed in scope
data_required: Stadium, roof type, historical weather, closing totals
what_would_kill_it: Cannot be verified at all with current sources; do not promote until a feed exists.

name: Rest-designation fade (JAX-style 'not injury related - resting')
thesis: A starter ruled Out for rest is a real availability loss that the report flags explicitly.
signal_inputs: S01 rows carrying 'Not injury related - resting player'
data_required: Injury report + depth charts + team totals
why_it_might_work: The designation is official, so detection is objective (2 such rows observed in Week 10: Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis).
what_would_kill_it: Rest is often announced early, so it is likely already in the price.

name: Originated-line divergence (our number vs the close)
thesis: Build our own power ratings, originate a line, and bet only when our number differs from the close beyond a calibrated threshold.
data_required: Team stats + closing lines + full season history
why_it_might_work: This is the cleanest, most auditable path: no proprietary data needed.
what_would_kill_it: Without an odds archive we cannot calibrate the threshold, and the market is efficient enough (Q11) that the threshold may be unreachable.
